causal_chain: A conflict gate chooses between direct user-item affinity and transported state evidence when scoring candidates.
A user is represented by a small set of persistent latent preference states instead of one static vector.
Each observed pairwise interaction updates the state bank through event-conditioned transport, so repeated evidence can accumulate in different taste modes.
This should better preserve minority or short-lived intents at full-sort ranking time than a single-embedding collaborative filter.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Single-embedding pairwise matrix factorization is sufficient; any gains come from better optimization of the same static compatibility signal rather than from state transport or conflict gating.
discriminative_predictions: A plain BPR-MF control should not replicate the same pattern of gains when tail or substitute items are supported by different latent states.
If the mechanism is right, ablations that remove state transport or the conflict gate should hurt users with high intra-history disagreement more than users with homogeneous histories.
Score changes should track candidate support from the user's recent minority-interest states, not just global user-item dot-product strength.
expected_evidence: Higher full-sort NDCG@10 than the matched static BPR control under the frozen split.
Largest relative improvements concentrated on users whose history appears multi-modal under the learned state assignments.
Transport and gate activations should be nontrivial and structured rather than collapsing to a single always-on path.
research_spec.falsifier: If the model does not outperform the matched BPR-MF control and the learned state transport/gating collapses to a near-static user embedding behavior, the proposed mechanism is not adding useful ranking signal.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This is a high-change front-end because it changes the core representation from one user vector to a multi-state user memory, changes the interaction structure from static affinity to routed evidence, and adds a propagation-like transport mechanism over pairwise events.
research_spec.hypothesis: A conflict-gated multi-state transport recommender will generalize better than a static collaborative filter because it can separate stable preferences from contradictory evidence and reuse the right latent state at ranking time.
implementation_requirements: conflict gate over direct vs transported scores
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use the same frozen ML-1M split, embedding budget, optimizer family, and full-sort evaluator, but replace the transport/gating block with plain BPR-MF.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a small persistent user-state bank updated by pairwise event-conditioned transport, then score candidates by a conflict gate blending direct affinity and transported evidence.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Collapse to standard BPR-MF with one static user embedding, one item embedding, no transport, no gate, and no extra state memory.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: Compare the proposed model against a matched BPR-MF baseline and an ablation with transport removed but gate retained, using the same frozen split and full-sort NDCG@10.
research_spec.research_question: Can a pairwise-trained recommender that routes each user through a small set of persistent preference states with conflict-gated transport outperform a static single-embedding collaborative filter on ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 under the frozen protocol?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The mechanism should fit the budget because it adds only a lightweight per-user state bank and small routing module on top of pairwise training, so qualification should remain within the 10 GPU-minute envelope on ML-1M.
